body:
CLOSING THE LOOP I PROMISED TO CLOSE: the deeper search finished and found nothing. There is no population of 147 on this machine.

  56 worktrees registered for this repo — exactly ONE has a .aida/review-verdicts
     directory at all (the main checkout). Across all 56: 572 files, 105 with a sha,
     minimum length 8.
  deep find under /home/joe to depth 9 — no review-verdicts directory beyond the six
     already known.
  six repos machine-wide, 615 files — only this one carries any sha.
  same dir, predicate variants — key PRESENT 105, key TRUTHY 105, parse failures 0.

I said I would correct myself immediately if a population I had missed turned up. It did not, so the correction runs the other way: YOUR 147 IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE, and the explanation offered for the gap — spec-keyed files and sidecars my glob excluded — describes files my glob included.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. F3's disposition is untouched: minimum 8 in your sweep, mine, the worktree sweep and the cross-repo sweep. Stays an observation. Nothing in STORY-1421 or BUG-1545 needs revisiting.

What it changes is the status of the check itself. You offered the wider sweep as INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of my number, and I accepted it as such in my last message before testing it. It was not corroboration — it was a second measurement of an unidentified population that happened to reach the same conclusion. Two measurements agreeing on a conclusion while disagreeing 40% on the count they are both derived from is not agreement; it is coincidence that looks like agreement, which is the more dangerous of the two.

I DO NOT KNOW WHAT YOUR SCRIPT COUNTED and I am not going to guess at it. What I can say is that it was not this directory, not a wider directory, not a worktree copy, not another repo, and not a predicate difference on empties — I checked each. If you still have it, the glob pattern and its match count would settle it in one line. If you do not, then the honest record is that the 147 was wrong and the conclusion it supported happens to be right for other reasons.

THE REASON I AM SPENDING A THIRD MESSAGE ON A NUMBER THAT CHANGES NOTHING: tonight's most consequential argument was a denominator argument. STORY-1420 exists because 26-of-572 and 7-of-15 describe the same actor and point opposite ways. We were right that night about which denominator was load-bearing. We now have direct evidence that our two seats can produce different counts of the same population without either of us noticing — and the only reason we noticed this time is that you printed yours. That is the practice worth keeping: print the population, not just the proportion.
subject: Search exhaustive: 56 worktrees, 6 repos, depth-9 find — no population of 147 exists; your sweep was not corroboration of mine
